selection: Primary papers, author publications/repositories and official engine/library/standard documentation. Mechanisms are hypotheses until measured against the current contract.

experiments.E5: Exact eligibility plus replication deltas/sharing/fair queues
experiments.E6: Bounded multicore ownership and end-to-end server
experiments.E8: Conservative GPU broadphase plus CPU f64 exact filter

sources.title: Interest Management for Massively Multiplayer Games
claims_supported: Interest management separates relevant recipients from full broadcast.
AOI strategy must be evaluated against actual world and movement workloads.
sources.limitations: Historical prototype and visibility/AOI semantics differ from this exact f64 radius API.

sources.title: Colyseus: A Distributed Architecture for Online Multiplayer Games
claims_supported: Primary-copy authority with read-only weakly consistent replicas.
Predictable locality and prefetching can hide distributed object discovery latency.
sources.limitations: Hundreds-player historical evaluation; weak consistency and game-specific assumptions do not demonstrate 20k capacity.

sources.title: A Scalable Server for 3D Metaverses
claims_supported: Standing query cuts reduce repeated traversal.
Conservative query aggregation exploits nearby queriers.
Static/dynamic LBVHs and solid-angle object aggregation support scalable discovery.
sources.limitations: Solid-angle queries and aggregate objects change radius-report semantics; static-heavy measured worlds are not all-moving crowds.

sources.title: Replication Graph in Unreal Engine
claims_supported: Persistent shared nodes maintain reusable replication lists across frames/connections.
Per-actor per-connection evaluation can be expensive.
sources.limitations: Engine-specific actor relevance; cited example is not a 20k connected-server benchmark.

sources.title: Iris Filtering in Unreal Engine
claims_supported: Filtering selects which connections receive an object.
Owner, connection, group and dynamic filtering are distinct eligibility mechanisms.
sources.limitations: Filtering policy does not implement this library predicate; documented feature status can vary with engine version.

sources.title: Iris Prioritization in Unreal Engine
claims_supported: Bandwidth prevents all objects/properties being sent every frame.
Priorities select objects considered for replication.
sources.limitations: Priority/deferral changes delivery age and fidelity; not an exact radius-query optimization.

sources.title: Ghost snapshots and synchronization
claims_supported: Ghost snapshot processing uses entity chunks.
Snapshots support delta compression and partial snapshots.
Network and simulation tick rates can differ and send work can be spread across connections.
sources.limitations: Version-pinned documentation; eventual consistency, quantization and partial delivery need explicit application guarantees.

sources.title: Optimizing your game
claims_supported: Relevancy selects connection/ghost pairs.
Chunk importance includes age and optional distance scaling.
Snapshot size/send limits and serialization checks have CPU and bandwidth consequences.
sources.limitations: Per-chunk soft limits and deferred snapshots do not ensure per-entity freshness; version-specific behavior.

sources.title: Spatial Hashing: Spatial Hash Interest Management
claims_supported: Grid locality replaces every-entity/every-connection distance checks.
Documented implementation sends neighboring grid entries.
sources.limitations: Neighbor-cell membership is not arbitrary closed Euclidean radius reporting; historical speedup is not transferable evidence.

sources.title: N-Body Problems in Statistical Learning
sources.author_or_owner: Alexander Gray and Andrew Moore, NeurIPS 2000
claims_supported: Dual kd-trees compare node pairs to accelerate all-point-pairs problems.
Geometric pruning/aggregation can share work across query and reference sets.
sources.limitations: Aggregation for sums/counts can avoid work that explicit ID reporting still must perform; no blanket linear complexity guarantee.

sources.title: Tree-Independent Dual-Tree Algorithms
claims_supported: Separates tree, traversal, base case and pruning rule.
Supports reuse of branch-and-bound reasoning across tree families and parallel extensions.
sources.limitations: Framework supplies no ready-made proof of variable-radius f64 bounds or workload-independent runtime.

sources.title: Efficient processing of spatial joins using R-trees
claims_supported: Spatial join treats two indexed sets jointly rather than repeating independent searches.
R-tree overlap filtering motivates paired hierarchy traversal.
sources.limitations: Rectangle joins and external-memory-era settings differ from point-radius CPU batches.

sources.title: scipy.spatial.cKDTree.query_ball_tree
claims_supported: Finds point pairs at distance at most a common radius.
Nonzero eps enables approximate pruning/bulk addition.
sources.limitations: Common-radius API; exact mathematical query meaning is not binary operation parity with the Rust oracle. eps>0 changes semantics.

sources.title: scipy.spatial.cKDTree.query_ball_point
claims_supported: Batched query centers and broadcastable radii support coherent range-query workloads.
Workers, sorted results and count-only results are independently configurable.
sources.limitations: Count-only output and sorting/worker settings must not be mixed with materialized-report comparisons.

sources.title: ST_DWithin
claims_supported: Index-aware distance search includes a bounding-box comparison.
2D and 3D predicates are distinct.
sources.limitations: Database geometry/geography and coordinate-system contracts differ; source illustrates broad/narrow filtering, not kernel performance.

sources.title: Box2D: Dynamic Tree
claims_supported: AABB tree uses pooled node indices, proxy move/enlarge operations and partial rebuilds.
Node/leaf visits, area ratio and bytes can diagnose quality and memory.
sources.limitations: Broad-phase AABB results require precise radius filtering; Box2D floating arithmetic and dimension differ.

sources.title: Dynamic AABB Tree
claims_supported: Dynamic hierarchy quality, incremental updates and rebuilding are practical broad-phase design concerns.
sources.limitations: Physics broad phase is not an exact point-radius reporter; tuning must be measured on this workload.

sources.title: Scene Queries — PhysX 5.4.1
claims_supported: Main tree refit plus secondary pruner supports additions during incremental rebuild.
Long-lived topology can degrade query quality; rebuild quality/build time trade off.
GPU broadphase does not automatically provide GPU scene queries.
sources.limitations: PhysX engine contract differs; excluding new objects through a disabled secondary pruner is unacceptable for immediate exact queries.

sources.title: Thinking Parallel, Part II: Tree Traversal on the GPU
claims_supported: Iterative traversal and query ordering improve coherence.
Simultaneous traversal may reduce geometric work but lose to execution divergence.
sources.limitations: Historical GPU-specific timings are not modern CPU/GPU predictions; all-pairs duplicate suppression assumes a particular collision task.

sources.title: Maximizing Parallelism in the Construction of BVHs, Octrees, and k-d Trees
claims_supported: Parallel radix-tree construction over sorted Morton codes enables parallel BVH/octree/kd-tree construction.
sources.limitations: Morton sorting, duplicate keys, build quality and exact boundary filtering remain costs; paper is not an AOI benchmark.

sources.title: GPU Gems 3, Chapter 32: Broad-Phase Collision Detection with CUDA
claims_supported: Sort/sweep and spatial subdivision expose parallel candidate generation.
Multi-cell overlap creates duplicate/conflicting-work concerns.
sources.limitations: Collision broad phase and CUDA hardware assumptions differ from exact radius reports on Apple/WebGPU.

sources.title: GPU Gems 3, Chapter 39: Parallel Prefix Sum (Scan) with CUDA
claims_supported: Work-efficient scan supports compacting accepted candidates into dense output.
Scan plus scatter can reduce transfer of rejected candidates.
sources.limitations: Multiple passes and synchronization must be included; compaction cannot shrink a genuinely all-visible result.

sources.title: WebGPU
sources.author_or_owner: W3C GPU for the Web Working Group
claims_supported: Buffer mapping is asynchronous and waits for GPU use to finish.
Mapped buffers cannot simultaneously be used by the GPU.
sources.limitations: Specification defines ordering rather than device latency; adapter/backend capabilities require measurement.

sources.title: WebGPU Shading Language
sources.author_or_owner: W3C GPU for the Web Working Group
claims_supported: Concrete floating scalar types are f32 and optional f16.
Floating evaluation and conversions have explicit portability rules.
sources.limitations: No direct runtime f64 parity with this API; AbstractFloat is not a general f64 storage/computation replacement.

sources.title: MTLStorageMode.shared
claims_supported: CPU and GPU share system-memory resources on Apple silicon.
Application must synchronize producer completion before the other processor accesses a resource.
sources.limitations: Shared storage removes neither synchronization nor contention; does not establish throughput or scalar precision support.

sources.title: Shared-nothing Design
claims_supported: One application thread per core and explicit message passing make ownership/cross-core communication visible.
sources.limitations: C++ framework design reference only; locality, load imbalance and cross-shard traffic must be tested in Rust.

sources.title: Userspace RCU
claims_supported: Read-copy-update supports concurrent read-mostly structures with deferred reclamation.
sources.limitations: C library and reported scaling are not a Rust implementation proof; epoch memory and reader lifetimes need explicit bounds.

sources.title: tokio::task::spawn_blocking
claims_supported: CPU-bound blocking tasks require concurrency limits because the blocking pool upper bound is large.
Dedicated CPU executors such as Rayon may suit CPU work.
sources.limitations: No fixed thread-count or latency guarantee follows from using spawn_blocking; running work must not be aborted for cleanup.

sources.title: rayon::ThreadPoolBuilder
claims_supported: Explicit num_threads bounds worker count and avoids dependence on changing default selection.
sources.limitations: Worker count alone does not reserve cores for I/O/simulation or prove parallel speedup.

sources.title: Scaling in the Linux Networking Stack
claims_supported: RSS/RPS/RFS/XPS distribute packet work and influence flow/CPU locality.
Queue count, flow imbalance and interprocessor overhead affect scaling.
sources.limitations: Linux/server-NIC specific; not a measurement of macOS or the current M2.

sources.title: Snapshot Compression
claims_supported: Delta snapshots must reference a baseline acknowledged by the receiver.
Initial state and changed-index/bitmask choices affect bandwidth.
Quantization is distinct from lossless delta coding of an agreed representation.
sources.limitations: Example compression ratios and data distribution do not transfer; per-client history, churn and packet loss need measurement.

sources.title: RFC 8085: UDP Usage Guidelines
claims_supported: UDP has no inherent congestion control.
Applications need congestion/rate/burst and message-size handling appropriate to their traffic.
sources.limitations: Guidance is not an application transport implementation or capacity guarantee; RFC notes updates including RFC 8899.

sources.title: Google Benchmark User Guide
claims_supported: Repetitions, warmup and random interleaving control common measurement variation.
Memory counters and reporting context help interpretation.
sources.limitations: Methodology reference; randomization does not remove all bias or authorize changing existing acceptance rules.

sources.title: Benchmarking tips
claims_supported: Repeated controlled runs help distinguish noise.
Low noise is necessary but does not eliminate measurement bias.
sources.limitations: Its process-disabling advice is superseded here by user instruction: never suspend/kill active workers; use an isolated host later.

sources.title: wrk2: A constant throughput, correct latency recording variant of wrk
claims_supported: Measure latency from intended scheduled send time to avoid coordinated omission.
Offered constant load differs from a response-paced closed loop.
sources.limitations: HTTP implementation and timing granularity are not a game-server harness; reuse the measurement principle, not claimed capacity.

sources.title: HdrHistogram: A High Dynamic Range Histogram
claims_supported: Histogram footprint depends on configured range/precision rather than sample count.
Latency distributions can be retained without unbounded raw samples.
sources.limitations: Quantization/overflow range and merge semantics need configuration; old recording nanosecond figures are not current-machine evidence.
